items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to expanding the scope of
the CHAMP program to include representation for other agencies whose
populations are impacted
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8057

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to expanding the
scope of the CHAMP program to include representation for other agencies
whose populations are impacted

 
PURPOSE:

Expands the scope of the CHAMP program to include representation for
other agencies whose populations face additional barriers to care.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the mental hygiene law to provide that the CHAMP
program includes representatives from various agencies whose populations
are impacted by substance use disorder and/or mental illness. These
agencies shall include but are not limited to the division of veterans'
services, the office for people with developmental disabilities, the
office of children and family services, the department of corrections,
or providers contracted by such agencies to provide assistance to the
impacted population.

Section 3: States the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2018 the Community Health Access to Addiction and Mental Health
Project (CHAMP) created an ombudsman program helping individuals access
treatment and insurance coverage for the services they require. This
program has been incredibly successful in helping individuals navigate
this complicated system. The CHAMP program can help investigate and
resolve complaints and violations of rights. It represents individuals
and helps advocate for access to treatment, denial of services, access
to medication, parity/coverage, discrimination issues, system naviga-
tion, medical benefits, enrollment referral, legal assistance for insur-
ance appeals.

This bill seeks to include representatives from various agencies includ-
ing but not limited to the division of veterans' services, the office
for people with developmental disabilities, the office of children and
family services, and the department of corrections to the existing
program.

Individuals who primarily interact with these agencies frequently face
additional challenges in accessing the mental health and substance use
services they need. Expansion of agency representation in the CHAMP
program will help more individuals overcome additional barriers they
face as a result of their unique needs.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to providing outreach

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8057A

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to providing
outreach services to make certain stakeholders aware of the independent
substance use disorder and mental health ombudsman program

 
PURPOSE:

Provides outreach services to make certain stakeholders aware of the
independent substance use disorder and mental health ombudsman program

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the mental hygiene law by providing that OASAS in
Consultation with OM H provide annual outreach services to other state
and local entities, including but not limited to the division of veter-
ans' services, the office of people with developmental disabilities, the
office of children and family services, the department of corrections,
or providers contracted by such agencies to provide assistance to the
impacted populations to make them aware of the independent substance use
disorder and mental health ombudsman program and the assistance they
provide.

Section 3: States the effective date.

Project (CHAMP) created an ombudsman program helping individuals access
treatment and insurance coverage for the services they require. This
program has been incredibly successful in helping individuals navigate
this complicated system. The CHAMP program can help investigate and
resolve complaints and violations of rights. It represents individuals

tion, medical benefits, enrollment referral, legal assistance for insur-
ance appeals.

This bill seeks to include representatives from various agencies includ-

for people with developmental disabilities, the office of children and

program.

Individuals who primarily interact with these agencies frequently face

New bill.

To be determined.

This act shall take effect immediately.
